task: Implement normalize_email(value). Remove surrounding whitespace and lowercase the address.

criteria.text: Remove surrounding whitespace and lowercase the address.

task: Implement parse_optional_int(value). Return None for a blank or whitespace-only string; otherwise parse the stripped string as an integer.

criteria.text: Treat blank and whitespace-only strings as None and parse other stripped strings as integers.

task: Implement is_valid_slug(value). A valid slug is nonempty, starts and ends with an ASCII letter or digit, and contains only ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens.
code:
def is_valid_slug(value):
    return bool(value) and all(char.isalnum() or char == '-' for char in value)

criteria.text: Require an alphanumeric first and last character and allow only ASCII letters, digits, and internal hyphens.

task: Implement format_name(first, last). Trim each input and join the two names with exactly one space.
code:
def format_name(first, last):
    return first + ' ' + last

criteria.text: Trim each name and join the results with exactly one space.

task: Implement split_tags(value) for a string. Split on commas, trim each tag, and omit empty tags.
code:
def split_tags(value):
    return [part.strip() for part in value.split(',') if part.strip()]

criteria.text: Return trimmed nonempty comma-separated tags in their original order.

task: Implement initials(name) for a string containing ASCII letters and whitespace. Return the uppercase first character of each whitespace-separated name part, with no separators.
code:
def initials(name):
    return ''.join(part[0].upper() for part in name.split())

criteria.text: Ignore repeated surrounding or internal whitespace and concatenate uppercase initials in order.

task: Implement contains_half_open(start, end, value) for a valid half-open interval with finite real endpoints and start <= end.
code:
def contains_half_open(start, end, value):
    return start <= value <= end

criteria.text: Include the start and exclude the end of the half-open interval.

task: Implement overlaps_half_open(first_start, first_end, second_start, second_end) for two valid half-open intervals with finite endpoints and start <= end. Intervals that only touch do not overlap.
code:
def overlaps_half_open(first_start, first_end, second_start, second_end):
    return first_start <= second_end and second_start <= first_end

criteria.text: Return true only when the half-open intervals share at least one point; touching endpoints alone are not overlap.

task: Implement split_intervals(length, block_size). Assume length is a nonnegative integer and block_size is a positive integer. Partition positions from zero to length into consecutive blocks, retaining a final partial block.
code:
def split_intervals(length, block_size):
    return [[start, start + block_size] for start in range(0, length - block_size + 1, block_size)]

criteria.text: Cover all positions from zero to length, including a final partial block when needed.

task: Implement intersection_length(first_start, first_end, second_start, second_end) for valid half-open intervals with finite endpoints and start <= end. Return zero when they are disjoint.
code:
def intersection_length(first_start, first_end, second_start, second_end):
    return min(first_end, second_end) - max(first_start, second_start)

criteria.text: Return the shared interval length, or zero rather than a negative value when disjoint.

task: Implement adjacent(first_start, first_end, second_start, second_end) for valid half-open intervals with start <= end. Return true when one interval ends exactly where the other begins.
code:
def adjacent(first_start, first_end, second_start, second_end):
    return first_end == second_start or second_end == first_start

criteria.text: Recognize either endpoint ordering as adjacent and reject separated intervals.

task: Implement clip_interval(start, end, lower, upper). Assume start <= end, lower <= upper, and the source interval intersects the inclusive bounds [lower, upper]. Return the clipped interval.
code:
def clip_interval(start, end, lower, upper):
    return [max(start, lower), min(end, upper)]

criteria.text: Raise the start to at least lower and lower the end to at most upper.

task: Implement page_count(total_items, page_size). Assume total_items is a nonnegative integer and page_size is a positive integer. Return the number of pages needed to hold all items, using zero pages for zero items.
code:
def page_count(total_items, page_size):
    return total_items // page_size

criteria.text: Return the ceiling of total_items divided by page_size, with zero for no items.

task: Implement page(items, page_number, page_size). Assume page_number and page_size are positive integers. Page numbering is one-based. Return the requested page or an empty list when it is beyond the end.

criteria.text: Use one-based page numbering and return only the requested page's items.

task: Implement sum_by_key(records, key). Assume present values are finite real numbers. Sum every numeric value found at key, including negative and zero values; ignore records without the key.
code:
def sum_by_key(records, key):
    return sum(record[key] for record in records if key in record and record[key] > 0)

criteria.text: Include all present numeric values, including negatives and zero, and ignore missing keys.

task: Implement index_first(records, key). Assume records are mappings and key values are hashable. Return a dictionary from each key value to its first record; later duplicate keys must not replace the first record.
code:
def index_first(records, key):
    return {record[key]: record for record in records}

criteria.text: Keep the first record associated with each key, ignoring later duplicates.

task: Implement records_with_key(records, key). Assume each record is a mapping. Return the records containing key in their original order without modifying them.
code:
def records_with_key(records, key):
    return [record for record in records if key in record]

criteria.text: Keep every record that contains key, preserve input order, and leave records unchanged.

task: Implement count_by_key(records, key). Assume records are mappings and present key values are hashable. Return a dictionary counting records by the value at key; ignore records without that key.

criteria.text: Count each present key value once per record and ignore records without the key.
